findings.name: collector_down
findings.detail: Two runs dead in seconds with no logs; get_job_logs answers HTTP 404 for both, so no runner was ever allocated. Same signature as 2026-09-05 and 2026-09-06.
findings.cause: almost certainly the Actions spending cap. PR #62, merged today, records the repository at 90% of a USD 10 monthly budget with 19 days left in the cycle, and moved Windows CI to opt-in for that reason.
findings.us_close_not_dispatched_because: the first dispatch established the failure mode; a second identical dispatch cannot succeed while the cap holds
findings.what_stops: every sweep, every paper-book mark, and the Petronas Chemicals measurement
findings.remedy: only the account can lift it - Settings then Billing then Actions spending limit - or it clears at the cycle reset

findings.name: mis_dating_now_self_labelled
findings.detail: the pack marks each affected row MIS-DATED, names the instrument and the proxy, and prints a count line. Three pages had to find this by hand. Neither refusing nor falling back silently: labelling.

findings.name: pchem_query_fix_measured
findings.status: open question answered, against the prediction
findings.detail: the widened Google News query first ran in the 2026-09-11 13:37 bursa_close sweep. MYX:5183 went from 0 articles ever to 2. Both are www.moomoo.com posts titled '$PCHEM (5183.MY)$' with empty bodies, neither escalated; the second is promotional spam.
findings.conclusion: 'PCHEM' matches the ticker-tag convention of retail social platforms, not the form the Malaysian business press prints. The query defect was real and is fixed; the coverage claim built on it is not supported. The name now collects noise where it collected nothing.
findings.next_test: a different index rather than another alias - nst_business, newly enabled by PR #62

findings.name: macro_staleness_resolved
findings.detail: the 2026-09-09 page reported 17 macro series past cadence, 12 of them DBnomics rows 436-497 days old, and carried re-sourcing as a purchasing decision. PR #62 settled it: the IMF never stopped publishing, DBnomics stopped carrying it, and FRED has the same PCPS series current. Now 2 series past cadence.
findings.cost: DBN:ALUMINIUM_USD read 2,525.96 at 2025-06 against FRED PALUMUSDM 3,158.27 for 2026-07; Press Metal is an aluminium smelter, so its main input price read about a quarter below market in every valuation of that name

lessons: A fix can work exactly as designed and still not deliver the benefit it was justified by; verifying the mechanism is not verifying the claim.
Where a number cannot be trusted, labelling beats refusing - the mis-dated rows carried a real return and only lacked a reader who knew which day it belonged to.
An aggregator going quiet is not a publisher going quiet; one route to a series is not evidence about the series.
Infrastructure has a budget and the budget is a dependency: a collector that cannot get a runner is indistinguishable, from inside the data, from a market with no news.
